(2) The use of agricultural materials that suppress the absorption of Cd and As by crops and the application of irrigation management techniques can lower the concentrations of these heavy metals in agricultural products.
the Cd and As contamination of paddy rice and other vegetables can be minimized by using a rice variety with low Cd uptake and by controlling the irrigation water.

the development of effective measures to minimize Cd and As contamination of rice and other agricultural products.
the development of effective countermeasures for Cd and As contamination of paddy rice and other agricultural products.
the development and application of effective measures for reducing the absorption of heavy metals by agricultural products.

the Cd and As contamination of rice and other agricultural products in Japan has been successfully managed by the government and farmers, and the contamination has been reduced to a negligible level.

the Cd contamination of agricultural land is a serious problem in Japan and the countermeasures are effective, but further studies on the countermeasure techniques are required.

the Cd and As concentrations in rice grains are affected by the management of irrigation water and soil, and the use of different varieties.

we can reduce both Cd and As concentrations by combining the use of a low-Cd rice cultivar with the application of soil amendments.
it is possible to simultaneously lower As and Cd concentrations in rice grains by controlling irrigation water.
